name: Major cyber incidents
summary: A ransomware attack on a Belarusian cloud provider disrupted businesses for days; no national-scale attack found
state: On 13 Nov a ransomware attack on Belarusian cloud provider ActiveCloud was reported to have disrupted client businesses for several days (The Record). It follows a second wave of attacks on supermarket refrigeration controllers in six European countries on 2 Nov, which no agency has attributed, after France blamed an IRGC-linked unit for October attacks on about 700 sites (The Record). No national-scale attack on power, health or finance was found as of 17 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Businesses using remotely managed building or refrigeration controls are most exposed. The NCSC publishes guidance for organisations on securing such systems and reporting incidents.
rubric_hit: Ransomware disrupting a large service (ActiveCloud, 13 Nov) = Watch; no national-scale infrastructure attack

sources.title: Ransomware attack on Belarusian cloud firm disrupts businesses for days

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
